papers.title: Exploring the bio-mechanical behavior of PEEK and CFR-PEEK materials for dental implant applications using finite element analysis.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study explored the bio-mechanical properties of polyether ether ketone (PEEK) and carbon fiber reinforced-PEEK (CFR-PEEK) as potential alternatives to traditional dental implant materials, such as titanium (Ti) and zirconia (ZrO2). Conventional implant materials often exhibit stress shielding leading to peri-implant bone loss and implant failure. STUDY SELECTION: Finite element analysis using a three-dimensional computer-aided-design (3D CAD) model of the jawbone with various implant materials (titanium, zirconia, PEEK, and CFR-PEEK) incorporated was implemented to assess the effectiveness of PEEK and CFR-PEEK. Two loading conditions (50 and 100 N) were applied in centric (case-1) and eccentric (case-2) to mimic the oral loading conditions. RESULTS: Titanium and zirconia implants were found to exhibit higher levels of stress shielding and therefore pose greater risks of bone loss and implant failure. Conversely, CFR-PEEK implants demonstrated more-uniform stress distributions that reduce the likelihood of stress shielding compared to their conventional counterparts; consequently, CFR-PEEK implants are particularly suitable for load-bearing applications. Furthermore, maximum strain values on PEEK-implanted cortical bone reached a state of adaptation, referred to as the "lazy zone" in which bone growth and bone loss rates are equal, indicating PEEK's potential for a long-term implant utilization. CONCLUSIONS: PEEK and CFR-PEEK implants are promising alternatives to conventional dental implants because they provide stress shielding and promote bone health. Improved stress distribution enhances long-term success and durability while mitigating complications, and highlights their applicability to dental implant procedures.

llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses dental implants, not hip implants or femoral stems; it does not quantify proximal femur stress in Gruen zones, micromotion, or compare intact vs implanted femur.

summary_zh.method: 使用三维CAD模型和有限元分析，比较钛、氧化锆、PEEK和CFR-PEEK植入物在两种载荷下的应力分布。
summary_zh.result: CFR-PEEK植入物应力分布更均匀，减少应力遮挡；PEEK植入物应变处于骨适应的“懒区”。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the biomechanical behavior of PEEK and CFR-PEEK as alternative materials for dental implants to mitigate stress shielding.
summary_en.method: A 3D CAD model of the jawbone with different implant materials was analyzed using finite element analysis under centric and eccentric loading of 50 and 100 N.
summary_en.result: CFR-PEEK implants showed more uniform stress distribution and reduced stress shielding compared to titanium and zirconia, while PEEK exhibited strain values within the bone adaptation 'lazy zone'.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through FEA simulation of dental loading conditions.

papers.title: Single-cell analysis of peri-implant gingival tissue to assess implant biocompatibility and immune response.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: The innate immune response, particularly the reaction of polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs), is crucial in shaping the outcomes of chronic inflammation, fibrosis, or osseointegration following biomaterial implantation. Peri-implantitis or peri-implant mucositis, inflammatory conditions linked to dental implants, pose a significant threat to implant success. We developed a single-cell analysis approach using a murine model to assess the immune response to implant materials, offering a practical screening tool for potential dental implants. METHODS: We performed bioinformatics analysis and established a peri-implant inflammation model by inserting two titanium implants into the maxillary region, to examine the immune response. RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis revealed that titanium implants triggered a host immune response, primarily mediated by PMNs. In the in vivo experiments, we observed a rapid PMN-mediated response, with increased infiltration around the implants and on the implant surface by day 3. Remarkably, PMN attachment to the implants persisted for 7 days, resembling the immune profiles seen in human implant-mediated inflammation. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that persistent attachment of the short-living PMNs to titanium implants can serve as an indicator or traits of peri-implant inflammation. Therefore, analyzing gingival tissue at the single-cell level could be a useful tool for evaluating the biocompatibility of candidate dental implants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于种植体周围的免疫反应和生物相容性，与用户的增材制造生物医学材料方向（LPBF、力学测试、疲劳等）无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not address LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing, fatigue, surface roughness, or any structural properties of implants; it focuses solely on immune response and biocompatibility assessment at the single-cell level.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估种植体材料的免疫反应以预测并发症
summary_zh.method: 利用单细胞分析和小鼠模型研究PMN反应
summary_zh.result: 钛种植体引发持续7天的PMN附着，提示炎症

summary_en.motivation: To assess the immune response to dental implant materials as a screening tool for biocompatibility.
summary_en.method: A single-cell analysis approach combined with a murine peri-implant inflammation model was used to study PMN-mediated responses.
summary_en.result: Titanium implants induced persistent PMN attachment for up to 7 days, mimicking human peri-implant inflammation.
summary_en.validation: In vivo experiments in a murine model confirmed the immune response.
